[[File:Vera Traub Oberwolfach 2021.jpg|thumb|Traub in [[Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in 2021]]
'''Vera Traub''' is a German [[applied mathematics|applied mathematician]] and [[theoretical computer science|theoretical computer scientist]] known for her research on [[approximation algorithm]]s for [[combinatorial optimization]] problems including the [[travelling salesperson problem]] and the [[Steiner tree problem]]. She is an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Vera Traub |url=https://people.inf.ethz.ch/vtraub/ |access-date=2026-05-19 |website=people.inf.ethz.ch}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Traub earned a bachelor's degree at the [[University of Bonn]] in 2015.{{r|x}} She completed her doctorate ([[Dr. rer. nat.]]) there in 2020, with the dissertation ''Approximation Algorithms for Traveling Salesman Problems'' supervised by {{ill|Jens Vygen|de}}.{{r|mg}} From 2020 to 2022, she was a postdoctoral researcher for Rico Zenklusen at [[ETH Zurich]]{{r|ethz|dfg}}, before taking a position as a professor at the Research Institute for Discrete Mathematics at the [[University of Bonn]].{{r|hml|dfg}} She joined ETH Zurich in 2025 as an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science, where, among other subjects, she teaches the course "Algorithms and Probabilities".<ref name=":0" />

==Recognition==
Traub was a recipient of the 2020 [[European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]] Distinguished Dissertation Award,{{r|dda}} and the Hausdorff Memorial Prize for best dissertation of the University of Bonn Mathematics Department.{{r|hmp}} In 2022 she received the {{ill|Richard Rado Prize|de|Richard-Rado-Preis}} of the Discrete Mathematics group of the German Mathematical Society, a biennial prize for outstanding dissertations.{{r|dfg}}

She was one of three recipients of the 2023 [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]], given to her "for advances in approximation results in classical combinatorial optimization problems, including the traveling salesman problem and network design".{{r|dfg|breakthrough}} She also received the 2023 {{ill|Heinz Maier-Leibnitz Prize|de|Heinz-Maier-Leibnitz-Preis}} of the [[German Research Foundation]], the foundation's "most important award for researchers in early career stages".{{r|hml}}
